chunks: What the Shaykh — may God the Most High support him — informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓala, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh (AS) about al-madhy [pre-seminal fluid], and he said: «In my view, it is nothing but like phlegm (al-nukhāma).»

key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: al-madhy: pre-seminal fluid emitted during arousal; in Shia fiqh it does not necessitate ghusl
key_terms.كَالنُّخَامَةِ: like phlegm/mucus (al-nukhāma): a simile indicating minor ritual significance, implying no ghusl obligation

ai.seo_question: Does al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) require ghusl according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓala questions Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) about the ritual status of al-madhy — the fluid emitted during sexual arousal prior to ejaculation. The Imam declares it comparable to phlegm (al-nukhāma), implying it is a minor matter that does not necessitate ghusl (full ritual bath), unlike maniy (semen). This ruling is a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for classifying al-madhy as distinct from major ritual impurity.
word_analysis: in my view / according to me
